create_patterns.name: selection-loaded-nothing-despite-explicit-keyword-match
create_patterns.content: In all 8 traces (t1-t8) the agent loaded no skill, even when the task text named the transform. Examples: 'Heat a tomato' (t2), 'Heat up a black mug in the microwave' (t6), 'cooled plate' (t3), 'clean fork' (t7), 'two spray bottles' (t5) and 'two sets of keys' (t8). The offered descriptions were generic one-liners, and every iteration scored val_f1 0.000. Loading nothing is the failure here, not picking the wrong skill. Fix: load the skill whose verb or adjective matches (heat, cool, clean, two). Use pick_and_place for a plain put (t1, t4).

create_patterns.name: selection-skipped-skill-for-simple-put-tasks
create_patterns.content: 'Put a salt shaker in the drawer' (t1) and 'Put a salt shaker on the black table' (t4) have no transform and no count, and the agent loaded nothing. These tasks need pick_and_place. A simple task does not mean no skill is needed. When no heat, cool, clean, lamp or two cue is present, the default choice is pick_and_place.

create_patterns.name: selection-ignored-cue-words-inside-long-task-text
create_patterns.content: The cue word can sit inside a longer sentence. Examples: 'cupboard beneath the sink' (t3) is a distractor, because the real cue is 'cooled', so the skill is cool, not clean. 'microwave ... cabinet above it' (t6) means heat. 'two sets of keys' (t8) means pick_two_obj_and_place. Pick the skill from the transform word or the count, not from the location nouns.
